bible_refs.note: The Greek text quotes Isaiah 7:14 nearly verbatim in the Septuagint form: 'Ἰδοὺ ἡ παρθένος ἐν γαστρὶ λήψεται καὶ τέξεται υἱὸν καὶ καλὲσουσιν τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἐμμανουήλ.'
The phrase 'Ἀνάστηθι, κύριε, εἰς τὴν ἀνάπαυσίν σου, σὺ καὶ ἡ κιβωτὸς τοῦ ἁγιασματός σου' alludes to Psalm 132:8 LXX: 'Ἀνάβηθι, κύριε, εἰς τὴν ανάπαυσίν σου, σὺ καὶ ἡ κιβωτὸς τῆς ἁγιωσύνης σου.'

choices.why: The noun ἀνάπαυσις is best rendered as 'rest' in theological context, contrasting divine repose with created seeking; alternatives like 'relief' or 'refreshment' weaken the antithetical parallel with 'you do not seek rest'.

The term παρθένος consistently refers to Mary as virgin throughout the passage; translating it as 'maiden' or 'young woman' would obscure the doctrinal emphasis on perpetual virginity in this context.

The compound θεοτόκος is a technical title; literal 'God-bearer' preserves the theological weight better than translations like 'Mother of God' which, while common, shift focus from her role in bearing divinity to her maternal status alone.
κιβωτός here parallels the ark of Noah and the ark of the covenant; 'ark' is the standard term for such sacred containers, while 'chest' or 'box' would lose the typological resonance.

The adjective ἀμάραντον modifies ἄνθος (flower) to convey imperishable beauty; 'unfading' captures the sense better than 'immortal' or 'undying' which would apply more to life than to a flower's enduring quality.

And you set in Bethlehem, the cave and the manger and the swaddling clothes; for in heavens you do not seek rest, but you yourself are the rest of the whole creation; yet on earth for us you suffer the things of the flesh; or did you not also endure hunger and thirst and labor? But you are the bread of life for the hungry, and you yourself are the river of incorruptibility for the thirsty, and you toil in the labors of the dry land's walk, bearing weariness apart from the sea's waves; 'Arise, Lord, into your rest, you and the ark of your sanctification'; the virgin, the God-bearer, is plainly evident; for if you are a pearl, then she is fittingly the ark; since you happen to be the sun, the virgin must necessarily be called heaven; since you happen to be an unfading flower, therefore the virgin is the plant of incorruptibility, the paradise of immortality; into which Isaiah proclaimed these things from God beforehand, saying: 'Behold, the virgin shall conceive in womb and bear a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel.' 'Behold, the virgin'; which? — the one approved among women, the exceptional among virgins, the honorable adornment of our nature, the boast of our clay, who has freed Eve from shame and Adam from threat, who has severed the boldness of the dragon; of whom the smoke of desire did not touch, nor did the worm of sweet passion harm her; 'Behold, the virgin shall conceive in womb'; whence, O prophet? 'I do not say', he says, 'for this has been guarded by Gabriel'; many divide the wonders of the God-bearer, yet many things are still omitted from them.

But I have believed in the offspring of the ever-virgin, Micah the place in which the wonder was done, David the time; for he himself 'From the womb before the morning star I begot you' placed in the prophecy of the Psalms; Gabriel therefore will say the whence; for he comes down from heaven, he upon this very thing is sent to the virgin, he in the time of the offspring comes along and necessarily is trusted to interpret the substance of the offspring; if indeed also from me you wish to learn, the following of the prophecy come near; and she will bear a son and they will call his name Emmanuel; what then is Emmanuel? 'God with us.' Therefore not God from marriage and corruption is conceived, and from a man and conjugal union to be begotten or incarnated.
pass_b_english: You have set your dwelling in Bethlehem—the cave, the manger, the swaddling bands—yet you do not seek rest in heaven, for you yourself are the very rest of all creation. On earth, for our sake, you endure the sufferings of the flesh: hunger, thirst, and toil. But you are the bread of life for the hungry, and to the thirsty you are the living river of incorruptibility; you labor in the dry places, bearing weariness far from the restless waves of the sea.

Arise, Lord, enter your rest, you and the ark of your holiness. The virgin, the God-bearer, stands plainly revealed: if you are a pearl, she is surely the ark; since you are the sun, she must be called heaven; since you are the unfading flower, she is the plant of incorruptibility, the paradise of immortality.

This is the virgin Isaiah foretold, proclaiming beforehand from God: 'Behold, the virgin shall conceive in her womb and bear a son, and they shall name him Emmanuel.' Indeed, 'Behold the virgin'—who is she? She is the woman worthy among women, the virgin set apart, the noble adornment of our nature, the glory of our dust, who has delivered Eve from shame and Adam from peril, who has broken the dragon’s pride.

No desire’s smoke touched her, no worm of sweet pleasure harmed her. 'Behold, the virgin shall conceive in her womb.' And when we ask the prophet whence this comes, he answers: 'I do not speak from myself; this has been guarded by Gabriel.' Though many marvel at the God-bearer’s wonders, many of her signs still lie untold.

But I have believed in the offspring of the ever-virgin, Micah the place in which the wonder was done, David the time; for he himself 'From the womb before the morning star I begot you' placed in the prophecy of the Psalms; Gabriel therefore will say the whence; for he comes down from heaven, he upon this very thing is sent to the virgin, he in the time of the offspring comes along and necessarily is trusted to interpret the substance of the offspring; if indeed also from me you wish to learn, the following of the prophecy come near; and she will bear a son and they will call his name Emmanuel; what then is Emmanuel? 'God with us.' Therefore not God from marriage and corruption is conceived, and from a man and conjugal union to be begotten or incarnated.
